Computer basics: first time using a computer?

This section assumes you are new to computers. Read one step, do that step on screen, then continue. If your screen looks different, stop and ask your supervisor rather than guessing.

Common actions and what they mean
Word or symbolWhat to doWhat you should see
ClickMove the mouse pointer onto a button or link and press the left mouse button once. On a touch screen, tap once.The button opens a page, selects an option, or starts an action.
TypeClick inside a white box where you see a blinking line, then type with the keyboard.Your letters appear inside that box. If the box already has text, use Ctrl+A only when you intend to replace all of it.
ScrollTurn the mouse wheel down, use two fingers on a touchpad, or drag the page's scroll bar.The page moves up or down. Long forms may have buttons at the top or bottom; check the whole form before leaving.
Search / suggestionType a few letters into a search box. Wait for a list. Click the exact matching row (not just the search text).The chosen name appears as a selected chip, row, or colored box. If it does not, the item may not actually be selected.
Dropdown arrowClick the arrow beside a field and choose one item from the list.The selected item appears in the field. Read it again before saving.
*An asterisk means the field is required.The record cannot be saved until the required field is correctly filled.
Save / CreateStores the information. Check the patient, company, amount, and record first; click once, then wait.Look for a success message, new voucher number, or saved record. Do not click repeatedly if it is slow.
Cancel / XCloses or discards the form. Unsaved information may be lost.Use only when you do not want to save the information.
PrintOpens the print window. Check the selected printer and preview before printing.A print preview appears. A printer may be shared; never leave patient pages on the printer.

Important safety rules

  1. Use your own user ID and password. Never ask a co-worker to give you theirs.
  2. Do not use the browser Back or Refresh button while a form has unsaved work. First use the page's Save or Cancel button.
  3. Before Save, read the selected patient, company, test, date, and amount aloud or ask a colleague to check them.
  4. If an error appears, do not keep clicking Save. Write down the page name and exact error; do not include passwords in a support request.
  5. Sign out using the account menu when you finish, especially on a shared computer.

Start here

MLab is a laboratory information and diagnostic-center management system. The visible workspace includes patient and lab-entry management, sample tracking, readings, receipts and payments, inventory, reports, and administrative setup.

Each detailed topic follows the same MLab help format: open the menu → click the action → fill the named fields → review → save → verify. Red numbered circles on selected MLab screenshots point to matching explanations beneath each image.

To see a picture clearly: select Enlarge screenshot above it. Drag the bar below the picture left or right, or swipe sideways on a touch screen. Select Fit screenshot to page to return. The red numbers stay on the picture. If the button is unavailable, use your browser's zoom or pinch to zoom.

Important: This guide explains software navigation, not medical or laboratory procedures. Follow your center's approved SOPs, applicable law, and the instructions of qualified personnel. Verify every patient identity, test, result, amount, and report before finalizing it.

Before your first workday

  1. Open the MLab website address given by your administrator in your browser (for example, Chrome or Edge). The sign-in page has three boxes: Organization / Lab Code, User ID, and Password. Enter the lab code supplied by your administrator and your own account details, then click Sign In.
  2. Confirm the organization shown in the header is the correct lab.
  3. Ask an administrator to configure company details, users and access rights, doctors, tests, rates, packages, accounts, and report templates before operational use.
  4. The left side of the screen has menu names. Click a name once to open it. Click Main, Masters, Reports, or System to expand or collapse that group. The search box at the top finds patients, tests, or entries.
  5. Use a training/demo environment for practice. Avoid creating test records in a production tenant.

After sign-in, the dashboard is the home page. To leave MLab safely, click your name at the top right and choose Sign Out.

Observed UI This guide reflects visible menu labels and screens on the live MLab demo tenant on 31 October 2026. Synthetic records are clearly identified as training-only and are not clinical or accounting examples. Some menus, actions, and fields can vary with organization configuration, version, or user permissions.

Dashboard: understand the daily and monthly overview

The Dashboard is MLab's home page after sign-in. To return to it later, click Dashboard at the top of the left menu. Use it to spot work that may need attention; it is an overview, not the source of a patient record, clinical result, or accounting balance.

Read the dashboard from top to bottom

  1. Confirm the lab and date: check the lab name and displayed date near the heading. If you have access to more than one lab, make sure you are looking at the correct one before using the numbers.
  2. Choose a time view: click Daily for today's summary or Monthly for this month's summary. The heading on the count, revenue, and patient cards changes with the selected period. Check the labels again after switching.
  3. Review the summary cards: the live dashboard showed Today's Entries, Today's Revenue, Pending Readings, and Today's Patients. In Monthly view, the entries, revenue, and patients labels change to This Month's; Pending Readings keeps its own label. The exact counting rules, such as whether patients are counted once or per visit, were not established. Treat the displayed values as a quick indicator, not a reconciled total.
  4. Check the charts: Account-wise Entries compares entries for company/accounts; Top Tests shows the most performed tests for the selected period; and Revenue Split shows top tests by revenue for that period. These are visual summaries; an empty chart or “No test data available yet” means no data is displayed there, not necessarily that the software is broken.
  5. Scroll to Recent Entries: the table shows Voucher No, Patient, Company, Date, Amount, Balance, Reading Status, and Actions. Find the correct voucher and verify its patient and company before using an action. A Readings button was visible; if it is available and you are authorized, use it to open the reading workflow, then verify the patient and voucher again. The exact button-to-record behavior was not independently tested in this check. Use the instructions in Readings. A row itself looks selectable, but that behavior was not verified.
  6. Search for a specific record: use the search box at the top of the page and enter an identifier supported by the search. Check the returned patient/test/entry carefully. For a full report or reconciliation, open the relevant report in Reports and confirm its filters.
Important: dashboard totals can change with the selected period, lab, data, and user permissions. Confirm patient details in Patient Entry, results in Readings, and financial figures in the appropriate source report before acting on them.

Typical daily workflow

The modules are designed to support a typical lab process. Your center's SOP determines the exact sequence and who is responsible for each step.

  1. Set up reference data: confirm patient, company/account, doctor, test, rate, package, and analyzer/machine records are current.
  2. Register the visit: create a Patient Entry, select the patient and required company, add the ordered tests or package, check any discount and save.
  3. Collect and track samples: use Sample Collections to find the entry by voucher or barcode. Confirm the test's specimen and container details against your laboratory's approved setup. The reason a training registration returned no sample card was not established.
  4. Enter and verify readings: open the appropriate entry in Readings, enter values under the authorized lab process, review them, and save according to permissions and SOP.
  5. Handle billing: record money received in Receipt Entry; use Payment Entry for outgoing payments. Check the party, reference, payment method, account, and amount before saving.
  6. Review: use the dashboard and relevant reports to check outstanding work, collection, finances, inventory, and audit activity.
Treat Save, Create, Transfer, and payment actions as changes to real records. Confirm the selected patient/company and the amounts before committing. If an action is ambiguous or a record may be duplicated, stop and ask an administrator rather than retrying blindly.

Live application screenshots

These screenshots were captured from the live MLab demo tenant on 31 October 2026 while following synthetic, training-only examples. They show actual application screens and populated fields; the example records and ₹1 amounts are not operational instructions or approved prices. Avoid copying any example into production.

In the step-by-step sections, look for the red numbered circles on selected screenshots. Read the matching numbered notes directly below each image, then follow the full written procedure. Markers highlight where to look; they do not replace checking the field label or your organization's SOP.

Some account labels have been hidden, but screenshots can still contain tenant-level summary counts and other contextual information. Review every referenced image for privacy before distribution, and keep this draft restricted to authorized staff. Unreferenced raw captures in the screenshots folder are not for deployment. PNDT website redirection is intentionally not covered.

The live gallery documents the workflows actually exercised. Other visible menus are described below, but their behavior and every field were not individually tested. Do not infer success or completeness from a menu being present.

Patient Entry (lab registration)

Patient Entry is the visible module for searching, viewing, and managing laboratory registrations. The New Lab Entry form includes a required Company Account and Patient, an optional referring doctor, quick-add health packages, test search, overall discount fields, notes, and Save/Cancel actions.

Create a registration

  1. Click Main on the left, then click Patient Entry. If you see a search page and a New button, click New. If the page says “No Record Selected,” use the page's New action if available; otherwise ask your administrator to check your access.
  2. In Company Account *, type the company/account name. Wait for suggestions and click the exact correct row. Check that the selected company appears as a chosen value before continuing.
  3. In Patient *, type the patient's name, patient code, UHID, or phone. Wait for results and click the correct patient row. Compare the identity details with the approved registration document. If no correct patient exists, an authorized user can use New Patient as described below, or create the record in Masters → Patients. Check carefully for duplicates first.
  4. Referred By Doctor is the referring provider. Type the name, wait for the list, and select the correct provider when applicable. A provider selection is not a substitute for confirming the authorized order.
  5. Quick Add — Health Packages: use this only when the ordered package is authorized. Search, select the exact package, and check the tests it adds.
  6. Add Tests: type the ordered test name/code, wait for the suggestions, and click each exact test. Make sure the requested tests appear in the registration list. Do not add a test merely because it appears in search.
  7. Overall Discount % and Overall Discount ₹ change the charge. Enter a discount only when authorized by the center's billing policy; do not fill both based on guesswork. Check the displayed total after any change.
  8. Notes is for brief operational notes allowed by your policy. Do not enter unnecessary diagnosis, passwords, or sensitive details.
  9. Before saving, read back the selected company, patient, referring doctor, package/test list, discount, and total. If any value is wrong, correct it before proceeding.
  10. Click Save once and wait for confirmation. Write down the generated voucher/entry number. Search it again to confirm you opened the saved registration.

Add a new patient while making a registration

Use this only after checking for an existing patient. The patient and the registration are saved separately. Creating the patient does not finish the registration.

  1. On the new Patient Entry form, search for the patient first. If the correct person is not found and you are authorized to create the record, click New Patient beside the Patient field.
  2. In Quick Add Patient, click Name * and type the verified full name. Choose the appropriate Title. The observed form has M and F controls; choose the appropriate available option according to the center's identity policy.
  3. Enter the verified Age * and choose the correct age unit from the adjoining list. An incorrect age or unit can affect patient identification and result interpretation.
  4. Enter Mobile, WhatsApp, UHID, and Address only as applicable under your center's policy. Verify contact details and use the approved identifier process; do not copy the synthetic UHID in this picture.
  5. Review the patient details and click the Save button inside Quick Add once. In the walkthrough, the saved patient was selected automatically in Patient Entry. Check that the selected patient is correct.
  6. Continue with the company, referring doctor, tests, charges, and review. Click the separate Save button on Patient Entry to create the registration; write down and verify its voucher.

First-time computer tip: typing a patient or test name may only open the suggestion list. Always click the correct suggestion. A selected item appears in the form; text left in the search box alone may not be saved as a selection.

Find an existing registration

  1. Open Main → Patient Entry.
  2. Click the search box that says Search entries by voucher, patient name, code....
  3. Type the voucher or patient identifier. Wait for the list; use Show all items only if the expected record is not in the short list.
  4. Click the matching row and check the patient and company before viewing or changing anything.
Patient identifiers and health information are sensitive. Confirm identity using your approved process; do not put unnecessary clinical details in free-text notes or share screenshots containing patient information.

Sample Collections

The Sample Collection screen supports lookup by entry ID or barcode, a Board view, Scan action, Stock shortcut, and filters for Pending, Collected, In Testing, Completed, Rejected, STAT, and Expired.

  1. Open Main → Sample Collections.
  2. Locate the registration using its entry/voucher ID or barcode. Confirm the patient and requested tests against the specimen label and your collection SOP.
  3. Use the Board or status filters to focus the work queue. Use Scan only with a configured, supported barcode device.
  4. Record collection or exception/status changes only when authorized, then confirm the displayed status.
  5. Use the Stock shortcut if your workflow requires checking sample/material stock.
Observed, cause unknown: the synthetic registration was searchable, but Sample Collections returned “No samples to display.” Its test had no Specimen Type or Tube / Container selected; we did not establish whether that caused the empty result. Check the registration, filters, permissions, and approved collection setup with an administrator and verify the workflow before operational use.
Sample acceptance, rejection, labeling, handling, storage, and recollection are laboratory procedures. Follow the center's validated SOP; the status names in MLab are not clinical instructions.

Readings

Only trained, authorized staff may enter or approve laboratory findings. The exact result boxes depend on how each test is configured. This guide explains screen navigation; it never tells you what medical value to enter.

Open the correct work item

  1. Click Main → Readings in the left menu.
  2. In the search box labeled Search readings by voucher, ref voucher, patient name, UHID..., type the Patient Entry voucher or patient identifier.
  3. Wait for the result list. Select the row only after checking voucher, patient name, company, UHID, and status. A reading voucher may be shown separately from its Patient Entry voucher.
  4. If you are starting a new reading and your role permits it, use the page's New action. In the new form, Select Lab Entry * is required: search by voucher/patient and click the matching suggestion.
  5. If the page says Read-only mode or “You do not have permission to create or edit records in this module,” stop. Ask your administrator to grant the minimum authorized reading permission; do not use another person's login.

Complete and check the reading form

  1. Confirm the patient name, age/gender if shown, UHID, entry voucher, company, ordered test, and department. If anything is unexpected, do not type a result.
  2. Analyzer Sample Code is an optional lookup/filter when the lab uses a configured analyzer. Use the exact sample code or patient name as your instrument SOP directs; do not type an invented analyzer result.
  3. Signing Doctor identifies the authorized signatory where required. Select the correct configured doctor; the referring doctor is not automatically the signing doctor. If the authorized signatory is absent, stop and ask an administrator to investigate the setup and access; the exact eligibility rule was not established.
  4. Lab Technician identifies the technician where the configured workflow asks for one. Select the actual responsible staff member.
  5. Find the test card under its department. Check its displayed test name/code before entering anything. Test Master offers Reading (numeric), Formula (calculated), Formatted (rich text), and Group (sub-tests). Follow the lab SOP and the on-screen configuration for that test.
  6. Enter only the measured/verified value in the configured result field, using the test's approved unit and decimal format. Do not copy the synthetic example or make up a value. For a Formula card, check the source test value and click Calculate; review the result and save the card only after the qualified check.
  7. Where displayed, fill Description or Suggestion only with authorized, reviewed report content. Do not use free text to bypass a missing test configuration.
  8. Review the result against the source/instrument and authorized laboratory verification procedure. Check patient/test identity again before Save.
  9. Click the form's Save action once, wait for the result, and confirm the saved status. A “saved” or “Auto-Verified” label alone does not establish that a qualified person reviewed or released a report.

Numeric, formula and group examples

The following values were invented only to demonstrate buttons in the demo tenant. They are not clinical results, reference ranges, or formulas. For a real patient use only measured values and the lab's validated calculation.

  1. For a numeric Reading, find the exact test card, click its Result box, type the verified measurement, and review the unit and range against approved source information. Add a remark only when authorized. Click that card's Save and wait for confirmation.
  2. For a Formula, check that the source test and value are correct. Click Calculate, check the displayed result against the validated formula, add an approved remark if needed, then click that card's Save. In the synthetic example only, 4 training points produced 8.00 from a demonstration formula.
  3. For a Group, open its card and inspect each named sub-test. In the walkthrough, one Group appeared as one registration row and expanded into two sub-tests in Readings. Complete and save the group only according to the configured test workflow and the laboratory's SOP; individual group-result saving was not tested.
  4. After saving, search for and reopen the reading voucher. Compare every saved result with its source. In the demo, saving both training cards made the reading show Completed and Auto-Verified even without selecting a signing doctor. Those labels do not establish clinical review or report release.

When viewing a saved result

The saved record shows the reading voucher, linked Patient Entry voucher, patient, entry/completion dates, department, test, result, and status. The live training result appeared as Completed and Auto-Verified, but the result text was explicitly training-only and not medical. Use Preview Report only when your role permits it; follow your center's release and communication controls.

Sample Collection returned no sample for one synthetic registration; the cause is unknown. Do not interpret that observation as approval to skip sample handling; the lab's validated specimen workflow remains authoritative.
Do not release or communicate a result solely because a value was saved. Result validation, authorization, amendments, and patient communication must follow your center's policy and applicable requirements.

Receipts and payments

Receipt Entry and Payment Entry have voucher details, date, optional patient-entry reference, party selection, narration, payment type/account, amount, outstanding vouchers, and previous transaction panels.

Receipt Entry

Use for money received from a customer/party. The screen supports an optional Patient Entry reference, a “Pending Only” filter, payment type, account, amount, narration, outstanding voucher allocation, and previous receipts.

Payment Entry

Use for money paid to a supplier/party. The screen offers an optional Patient Entry reference, supplier search, payment type, account, amount, narration, outstanding voucher allocation, and previous payments.

Record a transaction safely

  1. Open the appropriate module and select New if needed.
  2. Check the transaction date and optional reference voucher. Select the correct party.
  3. Choose the payment type (visible choices include Cash, Cheque, DD, UPI, Card, RTGS, NEFT, and Other) and the correct account.
  4. Enter the amount and any required narration. Review outstanding allocations and previous transactions to avoid duplicates or incorrect allocation.
  5. Verify the party, amount, payment type, account, and reference against source documentation. Save only after authorization, then note the voucher number.

Journal Entry is also available under Main for accounting workflows. Use it only according to your organization's accounting procedures and role permissions. The observed journal had a date, reference number, narration, account lines, line narration, debit and credit amounts, and a live balance check; save only balanced entries approved by your accounting owner.

In the observed demo, receipt and payment saves produced vouchers that remained Draft. Do not treat a save toast as proof that a transaction is posted, reconciled, or settled. Follow your authorized posting workflow and verify the resulting status.
This guide does not provide tax, accounting, or reimbursement advice. Reconcile transactions using approved source documents and accounting controls.

Inventory and purchases

Inventory Management shows Overview and Stock views. The overview includes total items, low-stock and out-of-stock counts, purchase totals, usage records, and category breakdown. Purchase is a separate Main-menu module.

  • Use Inventory → Overview to review stock summaries and low-stock indicators.
  • Use Inventory → Stock to inspect item stock. Check the item, unit, quantity, and location/context shown by your tenant.
  • Use Main → Purchase. The observed form includes Purchase Date, Supplier, Invoice No., Invoice Date, Invoice Amount, Bill Attachments, item search, Batch No., Expiry, MRP, Purchase Rate, Qty, Free, Discount %, GST %, Notes, invoice discount, and calculated subtotal/GST/grand total/balance due. Verify supplier, invoice, item, quantities, batch/expiry, tax, and totals before saving.
  • The purchase screen exposed keyboard shortcuts: F2 Save, F3 Save & New, F5 Search Item, Ctrl+P Print, and Esc Cancel. Keyboard shortcuts can commit or cancel data; use them only after checking the active form and authorization.
  • Bill Attachments displayed “Not available” during this check. Do not assume the application stored an invoice attachment; retain source documents through your approved records process.
  • Use Inventory Reports and Purchase Register for review and reconciliation where available.
  • Update stock only through approved purchase, usage, or adjustment workflows; never change quantities to “make the screen match” without supporting records.

Best practice: periodically reconcile application stock against physical counts and document differences using your center's approved process.

Other main modules

The following additional modules are visible in the Main navigation. Their presence does not guarantee that each is configured or enabled for every organization or account.

Appointments

Intended for appointment management. The current live screen produced an error; see Known issues. Do not rely on it for scheduling until the issue is resolved and verified.

Mobile Orders

Displays orders placed from the mobile app and provides All, Active, Delivered, and Cancelled filters plus Refresh. If no orders are listed, check whether a mobile-order integration is configured.

Bulk Registration

Builds multiple lab entries—one per selected patient—using a company and shared tests. Select company, optional referring doctor, patients, and tests; review the summary and final server-resolved rates. This can create many records at once: verify the list before choosing Create Lab Entries.

One synthetic patient/test combination was created successfully during this check. Verify the result panel and each generated voucher; do not interpret this single-item test as validation of larger batches.

Registration Transfer

Moves registrations between companies for a date range. Select From and To companies, dates, Load the eligible registrations, review each selection, then transfer only with approval. The screen states that completed and cancelled registrations cannot be transferred and that the destination company's rates are applied automatically.

One pending synthetic registration transferred successfully. Confirm the From/To companies, eligible voucher, and destination amount in the result panel after the action.

Patient, account, and journal records

Patient and account directories are available from Masters. Journal Entry is under Main. Access and permitted changes depend on assigned rights and your organization's approved controls.

Masters and initial setup

Masters contains shared reference records used by daily transactions. Incorrect master data can affect registration, pricing, reports, and compliance. Restrict changes to trained, authorized staff and follow a change-approval process.

Keep clinical and contact details limited to what is needed.
AccountsCustomer, supplier, bank, and cash accounts. Review departments, categories, and sub-categories

  1. Open Masters → General Master. Select Departments, Categories, or Sub-Categories. The counters show how many records are active and the total shown by the page.
  2. Use the search box to find the required item. Review the parent department or category where shown, because Test Master uses this hierarchy.
  3. The page states that an inactive item is hidden from dropdowns. Do not change an active/inactive control unless authorized and the impact on existing tests is understood. Creating or deactivating these records was not tested during this walkthrough.
  4. Use Refresh to reload the visible list if needed. If a department or category is missing from Test Master, ask the administrator to check its active status and hierarchy rather than creating a duplicate.

Review or add an HSN/SAC tax code

  1. Open Masters → HSN Master and search for the code before adding it. Only an authorized finance/tax owner should define a new code or rate.
  2. Click New. The observed form requires an HSN/SAC Code of 4–8 numeric digits. Enter its approved Description.
  3. Enter the approved SGST %, CGST %, and Cess % where applicable. The screen labels IGST % as automatically equal to SGST plus CGST; ask the tax owner to verify that this matches the applicable tax treatment before saving.
  4. Review Active and all figures, then use Save only after approval. Reopen and verify the code. No tax record was saved or tax calculation validated in this walkthrough.

Create a patient record

  1. Open Masters → Patients. Search by name, UHID, or contact details before adding a new record to prevent duplicates.
  2. Click New. Enter the person's verified Full Name; select the appropriate Title, Gender, and Age, including the correct age unit.
  3. Enter or confirm the UHID according to the center's identifier policy. Do not copy the synthetic UHID in the screenshot.
  4. Choose Blood Group only from verified information. Enter Mobile, WhatsApp, and Email only when verified and needed.
  5. Enter the minimum necessary Address and City. Add Medical History only when authorized, verified, and required by the approved workflow.
  6. Review identity and contact fields, then click Save once. Search for the patient and verify the saved record.

Create a health package

  1. Open Masters → Packages. Search the package list before creating a new one.
  2. Click New Package. Enter the approved Package Name * and Package Rate (₹) *.
  3. Enter a short Description if needed. Keep Active enabled only if this package is approved for current use.
  4. In Add Tests, search for each test and click the exact correct result. Check the Tests in Package list, test codes, and displayed total/rate.
  5. Remove any accidental test using its remove control. Verify that every included test is approved and the package price is authorized.
  6. Click Create Package once, wait for confirmation, then search and reopen the package to verify its name, price, active state, and test list.

Create a doctor/provider record

  1. Open Masters → Doctors. Search the directory to avoid duplicate provider profiles. Use New only for an authorized, verified provider record.
  2. Select the correct Title, enter the verified Name, and choose the appropriate Type. The observed options were Referral, Internal, and Both; choose only according to the provider's approved role.
  3. Select applicable Department(s) first, then choose the related Category(s) if the form enables them.
  4. Enter Designation, Specialization, and required Qualification * from verified records. Add Registration No. only after verification by the responsible administrator. Never use the training provider as a real clinician.
  5. Enter verified practice Address, Mobile, and Phone only as needed.
  6. Set Visit Charges and Commission % only with written authorization and finance/compliance review.
  7. Use Auto-select in Reading and Auto-select Order only when approved for this clinician and workflow. Upload a Signature Image only with the person's authorization and your center's controlled signature process. Do not enable a regulated designation based on a guess.
  8. Review all fields and save once. Reopen the profile and verify the selected departments/categories and approved credentials.

Use an authorized signing doctor

  1. Have an administrator verify the clinician's identity, professional registration, qualification, departments, authorization, and signature policy before maintaining the record in Masters → Doctors. Follow the Doctor Master steps above; never copy the training provider's details.
  2. On the actual work item, open Main → Readings, select the correct lab entry, and locate Signing Doctor. Search for and select the authorized clinician if the approved workflow requires a signatory.
  3. If the clinician is absent from the chooser, stop and ask an administrator to inspect the clinician's setup and permissions. A synthetic referral provider did not appear during the check, but the rule controlling who appears was not established. Do not guess that changing the provider type or auto-select switch will fix it.
  4. Verify the selected signatory and report preview under the center's approval process. No real signature was uploaded and no clinical report was released during this walkthrough.

Create an inventory item

  1. Open Masters → Items. Search by item name, code, short name, or salt before creating anything.
  2. Click New. Enter the required Product Name *; add Short Name / Alias and Packing only when accurate.
  3. Choose the appropriate Status, Type, Item Type, and Color Type from configured choices. Ask the inventory administrator if classification is unclear.
  4. Select Unit 1st and, when needed, Unit 2nd. Enable Ask Dose or Decimal only when the item and stock workflow require it.
  5. Enter Item MID only if the workflow uses a verified identifier.
  6. Under Classification, select the correct Company and Category. Enter Salt / Composition and choose HSN / SAC only from approved item and tax information.
  7. Scroll through the rest of the form, verify all configuration and required fields, then click Save once. Search and reopen the item to check the saved values.

Create an account record

In MLab, open Masters → Accounts (Account Master). Choose the correct MLab account type and group; these classifications affect where the account appears and how it is reported. Use only MLab's own labels and your organization's approved accounting setup.

  1. First check whether the account already exists. Open Masters → Accounts, click the account search box, type its name, code, or phone, and select the matching record if shown. Avoid creating a duplicate.
  2. To add a new record, click New at the top of Account Master. A New Account form opens.
  3. Under Account Type *, select one: Customers for an organization/person that owes the lab; Suppliers for a vendor the lab pays; Banks for an approved bank account; or Cash for the authorized cash account. If unsure, stop and ask the finance administrator.
  4. Enter the verified legal/trading name in Account Name *. This is required. Check spelling and confirm it is not already in the search results.
  5. Fill Phone (landline) and Mobile with verified contact details. Enter Email only if it is correct and needed for the account.
  6. Enter GST Number only when applicable and verified against approved business documents. Do not invent a tax number.
  7. Enter the account's Address and City from a trusted source where your process requires them.
  8. Set Opening Balance only from an approved, reconciled starting balance. The form may display 0 by default; do not treat that as a confirmed accounting balance or change it to a guessed amount. Ask the finance owner to verify the amount and applicable accounting treatment before saving.
  9. Choose Account Group from the available list with the finance administrator's direction. The screenshot's Current Assets selection is an example, not a universal choice. Group classification affects accounting reports; do not choose a group based only on its name or copy the example.
  10. Use Mark as default account only when the finance administrator explicitly approves it. Setting a default may change which account is preselected in later transactions.
  11. Review account type, name, contact/tax details, opening balance, group, and default setting. Click Save once and wait. If you have not decided to create the account, choose Cancel; unsaved information may be discarded.
  12. After saving, search for the new account and open it to verify the type and details. Confirm it appears in the correct chooser (for example, supplier in Payment Entry) before using it in a transaction.

General Master and HSN Master were opened and basic controls inspected, but their create/change workflows and field-by-field behavior were not exhaustively verified. Do not infer a clinical, regulatory, or financial setting from a default value.

Create or update a test in Test Master

Only authorized laboratory administrators or qualified personnel should add or change a test. Test configuration controls billing, result entry, report layout, analyzer mapping, and specimen workflow. Use validated test definitions and approved laboratory procedures—never copy the training values or invent clinical ranges.

  1. Open Masters → Tests. Search by test name or code first. Open an existing row only when you intend to review or make an authorized change; use its Modify action for an approved edit. Otherwise click New. Do not use Delete to correct a record without the system owner's approval.
  2. Choose the appropriate Test Type: Reading (numeric result), Formula (calculated from other test values), Formatted (rich-text report content), or Group (a panel of sub-tests). The fields change with the selected type; follow the matching steps below.
  3. Under Basic Information, enter the approved Test Name *. Add Short Name / Alias only if the lab uses an approved alternate label. Fill the displayed Department * and Category * from the organization’s configured lists; choose Sub Category only when applicable.
  4. Enter the Test Code only if the form shows that field and the code is approved and unique. Do not copy the synthetic code from a screenshot.
  5. Enter a LOINC Code only when the code is verified and the lab uses it. For a Reading, set the required Unit * from the validated method; a Formula has a Result Unit, while other types show different fields. Add Method / Technique only when confirmed by responsible technical staff.
  6. Expand Billing & Pricing. The observed numeric Reading test form includes Default Rate and CGHS Code. Enter a default rate only if approved; verify whether the company-specific Rate Master overrides it. Use a verified CGHS code when applicable; do not make one up.
  7. For numeric Reading tests, enter sex/age-specific Reference Ranges only from the laboratory's validated source and the correct population. The observed form had Male Min/Max, Female Min/Max, and Child Min/Max, plus Critical Low and Critical High. Qualified staff must validate all values, units, age definitions, and critical limits before enabling the test.
  8. Under Display & Suggestions, review the Reading Detail Template, Default Suggestion, and Report Footer. For a Formatted test, fill Description / Report Content and any applicable suggestion/footer only with approved, reviewed report text. The training screenshot contains explicit “TRAINING ONLY” text and must not be used as live report content.
  9. Under Billing & Limits, review Default Rate, Daily Limit, and TAT (Hours) where shown. Enter turnaround time/limits only from approved operating rules; do not assume “Unlimited” or a displayed default is correct for your lab.
  10. Use Print on New Page only when report layout requires a page break. Use Add to Quick List only when the test should be offered in that quick-selection list. Confirm intended effect with the administrator before enabling either option.
  11. In optional Machine Analyzer, select the configured Analyzer only when the instrument integration has been validated. Enter its exact Analyzer Test Code from the instrument mapping. Leave it unconfigured when the test is not analyzer-connected.
  12. Enable Ask Extra Patient Details at Entry only if the workflow requires the shown LMP Date, Children count, and Husband Name prompts and this collection is approved for the test.
  13. Complete Sample Collection Information from the validated specimen SOP: Specimen Type, Tube / Container, Storage Condition, Min Volume (mL), Recommended Volume (mL), Stability (hours), and Inversions Required. Review Requires Fasting, Protect from Light, Requires Mixing/Inversion, and Sample Collection Note → Add instructions only as approved. Do not copy the default settings or example values from the picture.
  14. Scroll through the rest of the form. Review every remaining option and any required marker before saving. Save once, then search and reopen the test. Verify test type, name/code, unit, billing, ranges/content, analyzer mapping, and specimen settings with qualified staff before using it for a patient.
Do not go live from the screenshots: they show synthetic test names, training report content, placeholder/demo pricing and incomplete specimen setup. Reference ranges, critical limits, result text, analyzer codes, and specimen requirements must come from the laboratory's validated documentation and authorized reviewer.

1. Create a Reading test

  1. In Masters → Tests → New, click Reading. Enter the approved Test Name *, optional alias, Department *, Category *, and optional sub-category. Enter the validated Unit *, LOINC code, and method where applicable.
  2. In Reference Ranges, enter the approved male, female, and child minimum/maximum values for the populations your laboratory serves; the observed form marked Male Min and Male Max required. Add critical limits only from validated documents. Obtain the qualified review required by your SOP.
  3. Complete approved billing, report display, analyzer, and specimen options. Review and Save, then reopen the test to check its configuration.

2. Create a Formula test

  1. Choose Formula. Enter the approved test name, alias, department, category, and Result Unit where applicable.
  2. Under Formula Definition → Formula Expression *, click Insert Test, search for the required source test, and select it. Use the displayed operators and parentheses to construct the laboratory-approved expression. In the demo, Insert Test inserted the source reference into the expression.
  3. Review every source reference, unit, calculation, precision, and edge case with qualified staff. Save and reopen the test, then validate it using controlled examples before operational use.

3. Create a Formatted test

  1. Choose Formatted and enter its approved name, alias, department, category, and method where applicable.
  2. Under Description / Report Content, enter the lab-approved template using the editor. Review Default Suggestion and Report Footer; do not paste unapproved patient information or copy the example text.
  3. Complete the remaining approved fields, save, reopen, and have qualified staff validate the report layout and content.

4. Create a Group test

  1. Choose Group. Enter the approved Group / Panel Name *, optional alias, Department *, and Category *; add sub-category or LOINC only if applicable.
  2. Under Sub-Tests *, search by name, code, or category and select each correct existing test. The observed form required at least two sub-tests. Check each displayed name and code; use the up/down arrows to adjust order or the remove control only when needed.
  3. Review billing and collection options, save once, then reopen the Group and confirm its members and order. The demo Group retained both synthetic members after reopening.
  4. When a Group is added in Patient Entry, check the selected Group and charge. In the demo it appeared as one registration row and its two members appeared in Readings. Confirm actual charges and results under your own setup.

Collection options for a test

Set a company-specific test rate in Rate Master

Rate Master associates a price with a test and a company account. Confirm the approved price and effective billing rules with the authorized finance owner before adding or editing a rate.

  1. Open Masters → Rates. Search for the test or company first to avoid creating a duplicate rate.
  2. Click Add Rate to open the Add New Rate form.
  3. In required Test *, search and select the correct configured test. Verify its displayed name and code.
  4. In required Company Account *, search and select the correct customer/company. Check the on-screen note confirming the company to which the rate will apply.
  5. In required Rate (₹) *, enter the authorized price in rupees. The screenshot's ₹1 is training-only and not a real rate. Recheck decimal places and amount with the approved rate schedule.
  6. Enter Description only for a concise, approved explanation, such as a rate schedule reference; do not put confidential or patient information there.
  7. To use approved date-effective pricing, expand Date-Effective Pricing and enter the authorized Effective From and Effective To dates as applicable. Check the date order with the finance owner. The effect of leaving either date blank and date-boundary behavior were not verified; do not assume them.
  8. Scroll inside the form if needed to find Create Rate. Review the test, company, amount, and dates; click it once and wait for confirmation. Use Cancel and, if prompted, Discard only when intentionally abandoning unsaved work.
  9. Search the test/company combination again and verify the saved rate. Then verify the expected rate on a controlled, authorized registration before using the setup operationally.

Reports

The Reports menu visibly contains Favorites, Lab Reports, Collection Reports, Financial Reports, Accounting Reports, Inventory Reports, Purchase Register, Audit Reports, MIS Reports, and Custom Reports.

Run a Patient Wise Test Report (verified)

  1. Click Reports → Lab Reports in the left navigation. If the Reports group is closed, click its name once to open it.
  2. Open the report selector and choose Patient Wise Test Report.
  3. Set the start and end dates for the period you need. The live form also displayed patient, test, company, status, and other filters. Leave a filter blank only when the report should include all matching values.
  4. For a single patient/test, type the value in its filter and click the matching suggestion. Confirm the selected company and status are correct.
  5. Click the screen's report/search action once. Wait for the result to load; do not repeatedly submit.
  6. Check the report title, date range, patient identity, test, company, voucher/reference, and row count. The walkthrough returned one synthetic row. A zero-row result may mean the filters exclude the record; verify filters and the source registration before reporting a defect.
  7. Use Print or an export control only if it is visible and your role permits it. Confirm the preview and destination; patient reports contain sensitive information. Do not send them to an unapproved recipient.

Other report areas

These categories were visible in the menu but were not each tested end-to-end. Use the category matching your task, choose a narrow date period and correct company/status, generate the report, and verify its scope and totals against approved source records before relying on it.

  • Collection Reports: collection/receipt activity; check date and company filters.
  • Financial Reports / Accounting Reports: financial and ledger views; reconcile with authorized accounting records.
  • Inventory Reports / Purchase Register: stock and purchases; check item, supplier, and date filters.
  • Audit Reports: Activity Log, Data Changes, and Login Report; detailed instructions follow below. Restrict viewing to authorized personnel.
  • MIS Reports / Custom Reports: management views or configured exports; availability depends on tenant setup and permission. Favorites opened the Laboratory Reports page during this check; saving or managing favorites was not verified.

Audit Reports: Activity Log, Data Changes, and Login Report

Open Reports → Audit Reports. The page has three tabs. Choose a tab based on the question you need to answer: Activity Log shows recorded actions, Data Changes shows fields changed and their before/after values, and Login Report shows sign-in/session events. These are sensitive security and operational records; only authorized staff should view, search, or share them.

Activity Log — what action was recorded?

Use this tab to review actions associated with a user and application area. The observed filters are a start date, end date, User ID, an action selector (All Actions, Create, Update, Delete, View, Print, or Export), and a text Search. The table columns are Timestamp, User, Action, Module, Entity, and Status.

  1. Select the start and end dates that cover the event you are checking. The page showed dates in year-month-day format. Verify the dates displayed; timezone and date-boundary rules were not confirmed.
  2. To narrow the review, type the exact User ID, choose the relevant action, or enter a useful word in Search (for example, a module name or record type). Leave criteria broad only when you are authorized and need a wider review.
  3. Review the matching table rows. Read the timestamp, user, action, module, and entity together so you do not confuse similar activity on different records. The displayed Status is a recorded numeric status; use your system administrator's definitions to interpret it rather than assuming it proves a business transaction was finalized.
  4. For an unexpected create, update, delete, print, or export, record the date/time and entity reference through your approved incident process. Check the relevant source record and ask an administrator to investigate. Do not edit or delete a record just to make the log look correct.

Data Changes — what values changed?

Use this tab when you need to understand a recorded create, update, or delete of an entity. The observed filters are start date, end date, User ID, Entity type (the field gave Patient as an example), an operation selector (All Operations, Created, Updated, or Deleted), and Search. The list shows Timestamp, User, Operation, Entity, and Changed Fields.

  1. Set the date range first. Optionally enter the responsible User ID, type an entity name in Entity type, choose the operation, and enter a search term to narrow the results.
  2. Find the exact row using its timestamp, user, operation, and entity reference. Do not rely on a patient's name alone if multiple records could match.
  3. Click the row to expand its details. The observed expanded view contains a second table with Field, Before, and After. Compare each listed value to determine what the audit entry records. A dash means a before/after value was not displayed for that field in the row; it does not explain why.
  4. For an unexpected change, preserve the audit details according to your organization's process and ask an authorized administrator to verify the current source record and investigate. The audit view is evidence of recorded values, not an undo/restore control. Do not copy sensitive before/after values into an unapproved message or screenshot.

Login Report — who tried to sign in?

Use this tab to review recorded sign-in and session events. It displayed summary cards for Successful Logins, Failed Attempts, and Total Records. The observed filters are start date, end date, User ID, a status selector (All Statuses, Success, Failed, Locked, Blocked, Logout, or LoggedOut), and Search. The table columns are Timestamp, User, Status, Lab, IP Address, and Session.

  1. Choose a date range that covers the period to review. Check the range and the summary cards; the totals depend on the selected data and are not a substitute for checking individual records.
  2. To review one account, enter its exact User ID. Choose a specific status to narrow the list, or keep All Statuses to review every listed event. Use Search only to narrow further.
  3. Read the timestamp, user, status, lab, IP address, and session together. Success is labeled as a successful login; Failed, Locked, and Blocked are separate recorded statuses. Logout statuses are also separate choices. The exact rules that produce each status, and whether a session is still active, were not fully verified.
  4. Investigate repeated failures, an unexpected time or lab, or unfamiliar session activity through your approved security process. An IP address can represent a network gateway or proxy rather than an individual device; do not identify a person from that value alone. Ask your IT/security administrator to confirm it.
Privacy and safety: audit reports can expose user identifiers, record references, changed values, access times, session state, and IP addresses. Do not publish these reports or place their contents in this guide. Export, retain, or share them only when authorized and through approved secure channels. The live tab showed filter fields and rows but no separate Generate button during this check; confirm the displayed filters and results after changing criteria.

Example: Signing Doctor Test report

  1. Open Reports → Lab Reports, open the report selector, and choose Signing Doctor Test.
  2. Set required Date From * and Date To *. Optionally choose Signing Doctor, Test, Category, Department, and Status using the available dropdowns.
  3. Review the dates and filters, then click Generate. Use Reset only if you intend to reset filters, and check the dates and selections again afterward. Report generation and Reset for this report were not tested.
  4. Check report title, date range, selected signatory, rows, status, and totals against approved source records before printing or exporting. If anything is missing or unexpected, stop and investigate.

Purchase Register and its summaries

  1. Open Reports → Purchase Register. Set the date range and, when needed, select the supplier from the filter.
  2. Review the top cards and Purchase Register rows. Check each supplier, invoice, date, and amount against the approved purchase records.
  3. The page also has GST Summary, Supplier Summary, and an export control. A supplier-filter discrepancy was observed in the summaries; do not rely on those summary totals without independent reconciliation. See Known issues.
  4. Export only if your role permits it and the destination is approved. Verify filters and source records before sharing the file.

Report availability, export options, saved favorites, and custom report behavior depend on configuration and permissions. A report should not replace reconciliation or clinical validation.

System and account settings

System navigation visibly includes Report Templates, Analyzers / Machines, Settings, Admin Panel, and Menu Rights.

  • Settings → Profile: review your own contact and qualification details. A qualification may appear on reports. Change only your own accurate details, then use the page's Save action if present.
  • Settings → Password: use the password-change form and follow your organization's password policy. Never share the new password or put it in this guide.
  • Settings → My Modules: review modules available to your account. A missing module may be permission/configuration-related; ask an administrator.
  • Settings → Notifications: review notification options shown to your account. The page stated that preferences are saved per session and permanent configuration requires an administrator; actual notification delivery was not verified.
  • Menu Rights: administrators use this to govern which menus/actions a user may access. Grant only the permissions needed for the person's job.
  • Admin Panel: reserve user and tenant administration for designated administrators.
  • Report Templates: maintain report layout/content under the center's review and approval process. Verify test labels, units, branding, and authorized signatory details before publication.
  • Analyzers / Machines: configure instruments only with the responsible technical team's approved connection and validation details.

Change your own password

  1. Open System → Settings → Password.
  2. Enter your Current Password, then a new password in New Password and again in Confirm New Password. The change form showed a minimum of eight characters; use your organization's stronger policy rather than treating the minimum as a recommendation.
  3. Click Update Password once and wait for confirmation. Never include a password in a screenshot or support message. If the change fails, contact the administrator through an approved channel.

Report Templates / Report Designer

  1. Open System → Report Templates. Only an authorized administrator should open a template for an approved change.
  2. The observed designer has Layout, Style, Content, Sections, and Advanced tabs. Layout showed page size, orientation, margins, and a default-template option. Enter a template name and optional description as required by the form.
  3. Review layout, approved branding, test labels, units, signatory placement, and privacy requirements. Use Show Preview to inspect the design; the observed preview used example data. Have qualified reviewers approve a controlled preview before saving or making it the default.
  4. Use Save only after approval and verify the resulting template through a controlled process. No template was saved in this walkthrough.

Analyzers / Machines

  1. Open System → Analyzers / Machines. Search for an existing instrument before adding one. Pending Results opens the import queue; zero results were visible during this check.
  2. For an approved setup, click New Analyzer and review Analyzer Name *, Manufacturer, Serial Number, Department, Connection Type, Protocol, Bidirectional, and Auto-Verify. The form changes with the chosen connection type.
  3. In the observed form, TCP/IP showed Dump File Path; Serial showed COM Port and Baud Rate; File-Based showed Watch Folder and File Pattern; Manual Entry Only showed no extra connection field. Use the actual instrument/interface documentation and your technical team, not these names as a configuration recipe.
  4. Validate connectivity, mappings, imported values, audit behavior, and auto-verification with the responsible laboratory and technical teams before enabling use. No analyzer changes were saved and no instrument integration was validated here.
System screens were not configured or exhaustively field-tested during this walkthrough. Do not upload a signature, alter permissions, change analyzer mappings, or edit report templates unless you are authorized and the change has been reviewed.

Administrator guide: users and access rights

Administrator-only: changing a role permission can affect every user assigned to that role. Make changes only with approval, keep a record of the intended access, and test with a separate account. Never share an administrator password.

Create a user

  1. Sign in using your own authorized administrator account. Click System → Admin Panel.
  2. In User Management, click Add User.
  3. Enter a unique User ID * and the person's real Full Name *. These are required in the observed form.
  4. Enter Password * using your organization's secure onboarding process. The form showed a minimum of six characters; use a stronger password policy where supported. Deliver credentials privately and require the user to change them if your policy supports that workflow. Never enter the password in a guide, screenshot, email, or shared chat.
  5. Select the least-privileged suitable Role. The observed choices were Admin, Limited, Receptio (spelled this way in the UI), Standard, and User. The UI described User as view/print only, Standard as create/edit/print without delete, Limited as view only, and Admin as full access. Confirm the current role description before saving.
  6. Fill Title, Email, Phone, and Qualification only when applicable and verified. Qualification may appear on reports.
  7. Enable Technician only for the appropriate staff member and approved workflow. Upload a signature only when the person is authorized and the organization's controlled signature process allows it.
  8. Review the user ID, name, role, contact details, Technician setting, and signature choice. Click the form's save/create action once and wait for confirmation.
  9. Ask the user to sign in using the lab code, user ID, and privately delivered initial password. Confirm they see only their intended menus and can perform only their authorized tasks.

Do not create a second administrator just for testing. Use an existing administrator account for administration and a separate least-privilege test account to verify restrictions.

Edit, deactivate, and delete

  • Use the User Management list's Edit action to correct an authorized user detail or role. Review all values before saving, then verify access with that user.
  • When a user no longer needs access, prefer Deactivate and follow the organization's offboarding process. The recovery/undo behavior was not verified; confirm the effect before acting.
  • Delete is destructive. Do not use it as routine offboarding. Confirm retention, audit, and recovery requirements with the system owner before considering it.
  • Review Active Sessions when investigating access; do not terminate a session unless authorized and the user impact is understood.

Create a role and review its access

  1. Open System → Menu Rights → Role Permissions. In the Roles list, click the + next to the heading.
  2. Enter a distinct Role name and an optional description of the job. Review the name, then click Create. Use a training role only in a demo environment.
  3. Select the new role and wait for the permission matrix to finish loading. Review every module and action rather than assuming a new role has safe defaults. During this check an unassigned role named Guide Training Observer was created; all 144 displayed actions were off after loading. No user was assigned to it.
  4. Choose permissions only from an approved access request. The header offers No Access, Read Only, Operator, and Full Access presets; each can change many actions. Inspect the individual View, Create, Edit, Delete, Print, and Export actions across all groups before clicking Save.
  5. After any approved change, reopen the role and verify its matrix. Assign the role only through an authorized user-management workflow, if it is available in that user's Role selector, then verify the user's effective rights and test allowed and blocked operations with a separate account. Assigning the new custom role was not tested here.

Understand roles and Menu Rights

  1. Open System → Menu Rights. The page showed two tabs: Role Permissions and User Overrides.
  2. In Role Permissions, select the role you intend to review. Presets shown were No Access, Read Only, Operator, and Full Access.
  3. Review each module in the Main, Masters, Reports, and System groups. Permissions are split into View, Create, Edit, Delete, Print, and Export. Grant only actions required for the job. In particular, avoid Delete, Export, and System access unless specifically approved.
  4. Use a preset only after checking what it will permit. The preset's name is not a substitute for reviewing the module/action matrix.
  5. Use User Overrides to inspect the effective rights for a specific user after role defaults and overrides are applied. The walkthrough's training account showed Read Only across visible modules and could not create or edit readings.
  6. If the page offers an edit/save action, record the approved change, save once, and re-open the user's effective rights to verify. Then sign in with a separate test account and verify both permitted actions and blocked actions.
A separate least-privilege training user was able to sign in and view the Readings screen, but could not create or edit readings. This verifies that one restriction for that account; it does not prove that every module or action is correctly secured.

Other administrator areas

Lab Settings and Lab Maintenance appeared in Admin Panel. Their detailed fields and effects were not tested. Do not change tenant-wide settings or run maintenance actions without a documented change plan, approval, and backup/recovery arrangement.

Known issues and future development

The items below were directly observed on the live demo tenant during guide preparation on 31 October 2026. They may change after configuration or a software update. They are not a guarantee about every tenant.

Appointments: page crashes with “Invalid time value”

Opening the Appointments page displayed “Something went wrong” and “Invalid time value.” The page could not be used during this check.

For users: do not rely on this page to create, change, or confirm appointments. Use your approved alternative scheduling process and contact your MLab administrator/support with the time and page name.

Future development: investigate appointment date/time values and API data; validate missing/invalid dates before formatting and show a recoverable, field-specific error instead of crashing the page. Re-test empty, malformed, and valid appointment records.

Sample Collections: no sample card for the synthetic registration

The registration and formatted reading existed, but searching Sample Collections returned no samples. The test master used for this training example had no Specimen Type or Tube / Container configured.

Interpretation: the cause was not established. The missing settings and the empty result were observed together, but that does not prove one caused the other or that there is a software defect.

Future investigation: check registration data, filters, permissions, and the approved collection setup with a controlled test. If a configuration problem is confirmed, show a clear, actionable explanation instead of an unexplained empty list.

Saved numeric reading: reference range displayed incompletely

In the synthetic Reading test, the configured male training range was 0–10 and the entry card showed Normal: 0 - 10. After saving and reopening, the read-only card displayed Normal Range: 0, omitting the upper value. The saved training result itself reopened as 4.

For users: do not rely on that read-only range display for clinical interpretation. Stop and have qualified staff verify the approved reference range and the result using the laboratory's validated process.

Pending investigation / future development: investigate and correct the saved-view range display, and test applicable sex/age ranges and report outputs. This observation does not establish whether printed reports, range storage, or verification logic are also affected.

Purchase Register: supplier-filtered summaries disagree with rows

With the synthetic supplier selected for the same date range, the Purchase Register row list and top cards showed one purchase totaling ₹1. The GST Summary showed two purchases and ₹2 taxable amount, and Supplier Summary showed two suppliers. The discrepancy was reproduced without changing the supplier selection.

For users: do not rely on the filtered summary tabs for tax or supplier totals until this is resolved. Reconcile against source purchase rows and approved invoices with the finance owner.

Pending investigation / future development: determine why the summaries differ from the filtered register, correct the filtering or clearly explain the scope, and test all tabs and exports using multiple suppliers and date ranges.

Other empty lists, disabled buttons, or access-denied messages may reflect setup, permissions, or missing records rather than a defect. Record the exact message and context instead of assuming a cause.

Frequently asked questions

How do I add a patient and make a Patient Entry?

Search for the patient first. If necessary and authorized, use New Patient, save the patient, then separately save the lab registration after selecting the company and ordered tests. Follow Patient Entry and Quick Add Patient.

How do I enter and save a reading?

Open Main → Readings, select the correct lab entry, confirm the patient and test, enter only the verified result, and save the correct card. Formula and Group cards have different controls. Follow the detailed Readings steps and your laboratory SOP.

How do I create a doctor or choose a signing doctor?

An authorized administrator maintains verified provider details in Masters → Doctors. The referring provider and signing clinician are distinct. See Doctor Master and Signing Doctor; do not guess why someone is missing from the chooser.

How do I add Reading, Formula, Formatted, or Group tests?

Open Masters → Tests → New, choose the correct test type, complete its specific fields, and have qualified staff validate it. Follow the four separate procedures under Test Master.

How do I set the rate for a company and test?

Use Masters → Rates, select the exact test and company account, enter the approved amount, save, and verify it on a controlled registration. See Rate Master.

How do I add a company, supplier, bank, or cash account?

Search first, then use Masters → Accounts → New. Choose the correct account type and use verified details and finance approval. See Create an account record.

How do I create a user, role, or menu access?

Administrators create users in System → Admin Panel and review roles/actions in System → Menu Rights. Start with least privilege, save only approved changes, and test the person's effective rights. See the Administrator guide and Create a role.

Which report should I use and how do I generate it?

Choose the appropriate category under Reports, select a report, review its dates and filters, generate it, and reconcile the results. The guide lists observed report names and a signing-doctor example under Reports; most were not tested end-to-end.

Why does the saved reading show only part of its reference range?

One synthetic test showed 0–10 during entry but only 0 in the reopened read-only card. Do not rely on that display for clinical interpretation. See the range-display issue and contact the administrator.

Why does Purchase Register GST Summary differ from the selected supplier's rows?

A discrepancy was observed in the demo; the cause is unknown. Do not use the affected summary for reconciliation without independently checking source purchases and invoices. See the supplier-filter issue.

I cannot see a menu or action. What should I do?

Your account may not have the relevant Menu Rights, or the feature may not be enabled/configured for your organization. Ask your administrator to check your assigned role and the tenant setup. Do not share another user's credentials.

How do I find a patient or registration?

Use the global search for patients, tests, and entries, or use the module-specific search by voucher, patient name, patient code/UHID, or barcode where offered. Verify the patient's identity and organization before opening or changing a record.

Why is a chooser empty?

Check that the required master record exists and is active, that filters are correct, and that your account can access it. Use “Show all items” where present. Ask an administrator to verify setup; do not create a duplicate record without checking first.

Why are dashboard or report totals zero?

Check the selected Daily/Monthly period, date range, company, and filters. The current view may have no matching data. Verify the underlying source records before treating a zero as a reporting defect.

Why does Sample Collections show no samples for a registration?

Check the voucher, filters, permissions, and the test's approved collection setup with an administrator. One training registration returned no sample cards and its test lacked Specimen Type and Tube / Container; the cause was not established. Verify the workflow with a controlled registration.

What should I do if a page shows an error?

Do not repeatedly submit or retry a transaction. Note the module, exact error text, time, and the non-sensitive record reference; then contact your administrator/support. Never include a password, access token, or unnecessary patient details in a support message. For the observed Appointments error, use the alternative process described under Known issues.

Can I undo a saved entry, receipt, payment, or transfer?

Undo, edit, cancellation, and audit behavior were not confirmed for every workflow. Do not assume a saved transaction can be reversed. Contact an authorized administrator/accounting owner and follow the documented correction process; preserve the audit trail.

Does a successful save mean a receipt or payment is posted?

No. The synthetic receipt and payment saved successfully but both displayed Draft. Verify the transaction status and follow your organization's approved posting/reconciliation workflow.

Can I attach the supplier invoice to a purchase?

The Bill Attachments control displayed “Not available” during this check. Do not assume an attachment was stored; keep source documents through the approved records process and ask your administrator whether the feature is enabled.

What should I check before using bulk registration?

Verify the company, selected patients, shared tests, rate summary, and total number of entries. The screen states that shown rates are indicative and final company-wise rates are resolved by the server at creation. Use the feature only with authorization and verify the created records afterward.

How should I protect patient information?

Use an individual account, lock your device when away, access only records needed for your role, avoid patient details in informal notes/screenshots, and share reports only with authorized recipients using approved channels. Follow your organization's retention and privacy policies.

Integrate this guide into the Help menu

The English guide uses inline styles and small local search/language scripts. The shared screenshot-zoom.css and screenshot-zoom.js files provide accessible image enlargement. It loads images from screenshots/; the separate language drafts and their shared stylesheet are in languages/. It does not load external fonts, translation services, libraries, or tracking resources.

Simple link integration

  1. Privacy-review each image referenced by index.html and the six requested language drafts. Copy only approved, referenced images into a new screenshots/ folder; do not deploy the entire source screenshots folder, which contains additional raw captures. Copy index.html, screenshot-zoom.css, screenshot-zoom.js, and only the Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Tamil, and Telugu pages with their shared stylesheet alongside it, for example under public/help/, keeping their relative paths unchanged. Treat the language pages as partial drafts until they receive fluent-speaker and laboratory review.
  2. Add a Help menu item in the application's existing navigation that points to that path. Keep it inside the existing authenticated application shell if the guide is internal.
  3. Build and deploy the app, then test the Help link and confirm screenshots load with a normal user account and an administrator account on desktop and mobile.
<a href="/help/index.html" aria-label="Help and user guide">
  Help
</a>

Embed inside an existing help panel

If the application has a Help page or dialog, you can embed the file. Set a descriptive title and allow keyboard access. Prefer a full page where possible so small-screen users and assistive-technology users can navigate the guide comfortably.

<iframe
  src="/help/index.html"
  title="MLab user guide"
  loading="lazy"
  width="100%"
  height="800"
  style="border: 0"
></iframe>
Security deployment note: serve the guide over HTTPS and behind the application's intended access controls if the content is staff-only. Do not weaken the site's Content Security Policy to allow embedding. If policy blocks inline CSS/JavaScript, move those blocks into same-origin static files and update the policy narrowly rather than disabling it. Set iframe permissions and frame policy deliberately.

Maintenance

  • Review this guide whenever the MLab menu, workflow, validation, or role model changes.
  • Re-test the Appointments error after a software fix, then update the Known issues section with the verified outcome and date.
  • Have fluent speakers and qualified laboratory staff review each draft language page. Complete the missing translations before presenting them as full guides.
  • Replace example URLs with the actual deployment path. Avoid hard-coding credentials, patient data, or tenant secrets into documentation.
  • Keep the Help link keyboard accessible, visible, and named clearly. Check contrast and test the responsive layout at narrow widths.

MLab User Guide · Prepared 31 October 2026 · Menu labels and behavior may change by tenant, permissions, and release.
